$comment: THE hand-written part. Four packages -- ui, js, php, py -- are generated from this directory and are never edited. Meta publishes no machine-readable spec for the Graph API, so every fact here is read from its own reference documentation and probed against the live host where that was possible.
title: Facebook Pages

authorize.$comment: Meta takes the token as a QUERY PARAMETER rather than a bearer header. It accepts the header too, but the query form is what its own documentation and every error message use, and appsecret_proof has to go in the query regardless -- so putting both in one place keeps the request readable in a log.

proof.$comment: Quoted from Meta's own docs: appsecret_proof = hash_hmac('sha256', $access_token, $app_secret). An HMAC over the TOKEN, KEYED BY THE SECRET -- and the two are one swap apart, both are credentials, and both orders produce a plausible 64-character hex string. It is OPTIONAL until an app turns on App Settings -> Advanced -> Security -> Require App Secret, at which point every call without it fails. Omitting it would ship a connector correct only for the less secure configuration.

oauth.$scopeComment: pages_manage_posts to publish, and the TWO permissions Meta lists as its dependencies: pages_read_engagement and pages_show_list. None of the three grants reading a user's own feed or their friends, and all are subject to App Review before an app can use them on a page it does not own. pages_show_list was MISSING until 2026-09-04 -- the permissions reference names it as a dependency of pages_manage_posts, and it is also how a user token is exchanged for the per-page token this connector authorises with, so a grant without it cannot produce the credential the connector needs. Nothing reported that: the scope list is metadata a HOST acts on, so an omission here fails during authorisation on somebody else's machine.
oauth.$comment: The PAGE token, not the user token. A user token is exchanged for a per-page token, which is why pageAccessToken is scoped `account` -- one per connected page -- while appSecret and the client pair are `provider`, one for the whole installation. Getting that backwards would let one page's automation post as another's. Long-lived page tokens last about 60 days, which is what accessTokenTtlSeconds records; there is no refresh token in this flow, so a connection is re-authorised rather than refreshed.

$sandboxComment: CHECKED. Meta has test apps and test users, but no test estate for a real Page: a post to a Page is a post, visible to whoever follows it. The faker is the only way to build against this without publishing.
sandboxNote: Facebook has no sandbox for Pages. Anything this publishes appears on a real Page to real followers, and deleting it afterwards does not un-notify them. Point it at a Page you own and have muted before pointing it at anything else.
$baseUrlComment: The API VERSION is a path segment, not a header. Meta supports each version for about two years and then removes it -- an unversioned call silently gets the oldest still-supported version, so pinning it here is the difference between a breaking change we choose and one we discover. v25.0 (released 2026-02-18, retires 2028-07-29), moved off v21.0 which retires 2027-01-21. NOT v26.0, which is newer and lives a few months longer: v25.0 is what facebook-lead-ads and instagram-business already pin, and three Meta connectors on one version is worth more here than the extra runway -- drift between them is exactly the kind that is invisible until one of them breaks alone. The version appears in THREE places in this file, not one: the base URL, the authorize dialog and the token endpoint. Verified against Meta's v22, v23, v24 and v25 changelogs: no breaking change touches POST /{page-id}/feed, its message/link/published fields, page access tokens, appsecret_proof, or any scope above.

credentialFields.label: App ID
credentialFields.help: From the Meta app dashboard. ONE value for the whole installation.

credentialFields.label: App secret (OAuth)
credentialFields.help: The same app's client secret, used to exchange the authorization code.

credentialFields.label: App secret (proof)
credentialFields.help: Keys the appsecret_proof HMAC. It is never sent -- it proves the token rather than accompanying it. For a standard Meta app this is the same value as the OAuth client secret; it is declared separately because they are different ROLES, and an app that rotates one without the other should not silently break the other.

credentialFields.label: Page access token
credentialFields.help: PER PAGE, not per user. Obtained by exchanging a user token for a page token; a long-lived one lasts about 60 days and is re-authorised rather than refreshed.
